data.name: Fixed Sequence (Hierarchical) Testing

data.name: Graphical Multiple Comparison Procedure

Test hypothesis with largest allocated α
If rejected, redistribute α along edges
Update graph, repeat until no rejections

CR.name: Complete Remission
criteria: Bone marrow regenerating normal hematopoietic cells
Bone marrow contains <5% leukemic blasts by morphology
Absence of previously identified cytogenetic or molecular abnormality
CR.timing: Assessed at end of Induction II (for pediatric protocols)

CRi.name: Complete Remission with Incomplete Hematologic Recovery

CRp.name: Complete Remission with Incomplete Platelet Recovery

MLFS.name: Morphologic Leukemia-Free State
criteria: Absence of blasts with Auer rods

PR.name: Partial Remission
criteria: Decrease of bone marrow blast percentage to 5-25%
AND at least 50% decrease in bone marrow blasts from pretreatment

RD.name: Refractory Disease / Induction Failure
criteria: Two consecutive cellular bone marrow evaluations (separated by ≥2 weeks) containing ≥5% blasts by morphology
OR evidence of EMD at end of Induction II
OR persistent CNS leukemia after 6 intrathecal treatments
OR CNS leukemia at start of Induction II after treatment in Induction I

Relapse.name: Relapse (after CR)

morphologic: Reappearance of leukemic blasts in peripheral blood
OR ≥5% blasts in bone marrow not attributable to regeneration
In setting of recent treatment with 5-20% blasts, repeat BM ≥1 week later required
molecular_genetic: Reappearance of cytogenetic abnormality after documented CR
OR reappearance of molecular marker after documented CR
extramedullary: Cytologically proven extramedullary disease after documented CR

Relapse.date_definition: Date of first observation of >5% blasts in marrow

Unevaluable.name: Unevaluable
criteria: Aplastic or severely hypocellular marrow with any blast percentage
Repeat evaluation every 7-21 days until assessment possible

MRD_negative.definition: No detectable disease by flow cytometry at sensitivity ≥10^-3
MRD_negative.clinical_significance: Associated with improved DFS and reduced relapse risk

MRD_positive.clinical_significance: Higher relapse risk even in morphologic CR

MRD_conversion.definition: Change from MRD+ to MRD- between assessments

data._source_note: EFS/DFS/OS from AAML1031 Section 9.2.1; TRM/competing risks from BMT CTN 0901 Chapter 5

EFS.name: Event-Free Survival
EFS.definition: Time from study entry (or randomization) to induction failure, relapse, or death from any cause
EFS.censoring: Patients without events censored at last known alive date
EFS.analysis_method: Kaplan-Meier method with log-rank test for comparison

DFS.name: Disease-Free Survival
DFS.definition: Time from achievement of CR to relapse or death from any cause
DFS.censoring: Patients in continuous CR censored at last follow-up

OS.name: Overall Survival
OS.definition: Time from study entry (or randomization) to death from any cause
OS.censoring: Living patients censored at last contact date

RFS.name: Relapse-Free Survival
RFS.definition: Time from CR to relapse (deaths in CR censored)
RFS.censoring: Death in remission treated as competing risk

TRM.name: Treatment-Related Mortality
TRM.definition: Death occurring from causes other than disease relapse
TRM.calculation: Cumulative incidence with relapse as competing risk
TRM.analysis_method: Gray's test for comparison between groups

molecular: NPM1 mutated with FLT3-ITD low allelic ratio

high_risk_FLT3_ITD.definition: FLT3-ITD with allelic ratio ≥0.5 (high) OR FLT3-ITD with wild-type NPM1
high_risk_FLT3_ITD.treatment_implication: May benefit from FLT3 inhibitors, consider allogeneic SCT in CR1

post_SCT_CR.definition: Bone marrow myeloblasts <5% by morphology with donor chimerism
additional_criteria: Absence of previous cytogenetic or molecular abnormality

AML_criteria: Bone marrow blasts ≥5% by morphology not attributed to regeneration
OR blasts <5% with reappearance of same leukemia phenotype by flow
OR reappearance of leukemic blasts in peripheral blood
OR reappearance of cytogenetic/molecular marker present pre-transplant
OR development of extramedullary leukemia or CNS involvement
OR institution of any anti-relapse therapy (including DLI)
MDS_criteria: OR reappearance of pre-transplant morphologic abnormalities in 2 consecutive BMs ≥1 month apart
OR reappearance of pre-transplant cytogenetic abnormality in 2 consecutive exams ≥1 month apart
OR institution of any anti-relapse therapy

primary.definition: Failure to achieve ANC >500/µL by Day 28 (Day 42 for cord/haplo)
primary.additional: <20% donor cells by chimerism AND absence of leukemia relapse

secondary.definition: Initial recovery followed by ANC ≤500/µL for 7 consecutive days
secondary.exclusions: Not caused by relapse, active viral infection, or drugs

pediatric.assessment_timing: End of Induction I, End of Induction II, End of each Intensification

considerations: CRi/CRp acceptable as response in less intensive regimens
Lower intensity regimens may use different thresholds

APL.name: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia
APL.note: Uses different response criteria based on molecular remission (PML-RARA)
APL.molecular_CR: Negative RT-PCR for PML-RARA fusion transcript

survival_analysis.model: Cox proportional hazards for multivariable analysis

events.relapse: Death in remission as competing risk

power_assumptions.cure_model: Exponential mixture cure model may be used

INSS.name: International Neuroblastoma Staging System
INSS.based_on: Surgical resection and lymph node status

stages.1: Localized tumor with complete gross excision ± microscopic residual; ipsilateral non-adherent lymph nodes negative
stages.2A: Localized tumor with incomplete gross excision; ipsilateral non-adherent lymph nodes negative
stages.2B: Localized tumor ± complete gross excision; ipsilateral non-adherent lymph nodes positive, contralateral nodes negative
stages.3: Unresectable unilateral tumor crossing midline ± regional lymph node involvement; OR localized unilateral tumor with contralateral regional lymph node involvement; OR midline tumor with bilateral extension
stages.4: Any primary tumor with dissemination to distant lymph nodes, bone, bone marrow, liver, skin, and/or other organs (except as defined for 4S)
stages.4S: Localized primary tumor (as defined for stages 1, 2A, or 2B) with dissemination limited to skin, liver, and/or bone marrow (limited to infants <1 year)

INRG.name: International Neuroblastoma Risk Group Staging System

stages.L1: Localized tumor not involving vital structures as defined by IDRFs and confined to one body compartment
stages.L2: Locoregional tumor with presence of one or more IDRFs
stages.MS: Metastatic disease in children <18 months with metastases confined to skin, liver, and/or bone marrow (<10% tumor cells)

data.description: IDRFs predict surgical risk and guide staging

neck: Tumor encasing carotid and/or vertebral artery and/or internal jugular vein
Tumor extending to base of skull
cervicothoracic_junction: Tumor encasing subclavian vessels and/or vertebral and/or carotid artery
thorax: Tumor encasing aorta and/or major branches
Tumor compressing trachea and/or principal bronchi
Lower mediastinal tumor infiltrating costovertebral junction (T9-T12)
thoracoabdominal: Tumor encasing aorta and/or vena cava
abdomen_pelvis: Tumor infiltrating porta hepatis and/or hepatoduodenal ligament
Tumor encasing branches of superior mesenteric artery at mesenteric root
Tumor encasing origin of celiac axis and/or superior mesenteric artery
Tumor invading one or both renal pedicles
Tumor encasing aorta and/or vena cava
intraspinal: Intraspinal tumor extension (>1/3 spinal canal, leptomeningeal space, spinal cord)
multifocal: Infiltration of adjacent organs/structures: pericardium, diaphragm, kidney, liver, duodenopancreatic block, mesentery

CR.name: Complete Response
criteria: No evidence of tumor (primary and metastatic)
Normal catecholamine levels if previously elevated
Bone marrow negative for neuroblastoma cells

VGPR.name: Very Good Partial Response
criteria: No evidence of metastatic disease (except as noted)
Residual 123I-MIBG in primary tumor site only

PR.name: Partial Response
criteria: Metastatic sites: ≥50% reduction in measurable disease
No more than one positive bone marrow site
Number of positive bone sites reduced by ≥50%
Number of MIBG-positive sites reduced by ≥50%

MR.name: Mixed Response
criteria: ≥50% decrease in any measurable lesion (primary or metastatic)
WITH <50% decrease in any other lesion
AND <25% increase in any existing lesion

NR.name: No Response / Stable Disease
criteria: <50% decrease but <25% increase in any existing lesion

PD.name: Progressive Disease
criteria: OR increase of any measurable lesion by >25%
OR previous negative bone marrow now positive for tumor

curie_score.description: Semi-quantitative scoring system for skeletal MIBG uptake
curie_score.method: Skeleton divided into segments; each scored 0-3 based on uptake intensity

scoring.3: >3 lesions OR diffuse uptake (>50% of segment)

siopen_score.description: Alternative scoring method with 12 skeletal segments

data.method: Bilateral bone marrow aspirates and biopsies (posterior iliac crests)
data.timing: Diagnosis, after induction, prior to consolidation, end of therapy

criteria.positive: Presence of neuroblastoma cells by morphology, immunohistochemistry, or GD2+
criteria.quantification: Reported as percentage if positive; <10% defines MS stage

methods: GD2+ cell detection by flow cytometry

EFS.name: Event-Free Survival
EFS.start: From date of diagnosis or enrollment

OS.name: Overall Survival
OS.start: From date of diagnosis or enrollment

Local_Control.name: Local Control Rate
Local_Control.definition: Time from end of local therapy to local recurrence

TTBM.name: Time to Bone Marrow Clearance
TTBM.definition: Time from start of therapy to first negative bone marrow
TTBM.significance: Early clearance associated with better outcomes

INRG_pretreatment.description: Risk stratification based on presurgical factors

high_risk_features: Age ≥18 months with metastatic disease (Stage M/4)
11q aberration without MYCN amplification in specific contexts

response_timing.after_consolidation: High-dose chemotherapy with stem cell rescue

scores.5: Uptake markedly higher than liver and/or new lesions

CMR.name: Complete Metabolic Response (FDG-avid) / Complete Response (non-FDG-avid)
CMR.pet_criteria: Deauville score 1, 2, or 3 (no metabolically active disease)
ct_criteria: Target nodes/masses regressed to ≤1.5cm in LDi
Bone marrow: No FDG-avid disease in marrow

PMR.name: Partial Metabolic Response / Partial Response
PMR.pet_criteria: Deauville score 4 or 5 with reduced uptake from baseline
ct_criteria: ≥50% decrease in SPD of up to 6 measurable nodes

NMR.name: No Metabolic Response / Stable Disease
NMR.pet_criteria: Deauville score 4 or 5 with no significant change from baseline
ct_criteria: <50% decrease in SPD of target lesions

PMD.name: Progressive Metabolic Disease / Progressive Disease
pet_criteria: Deauville score 4 or 5 with increased uptake from baseline
ct_criteria: Individual node/lesion increase ≥50% in PPD from nadir
OR increase in LDi or SDi by ≥0.5cm for lesions ≤2cm

data.fdg_avid: PET-CT may replace bone marrow biopsy if diffusely positive
data.non_fdg_avid: Bone marrow biopsy required if clinically indicated

data.interim_pet: Used for early response assessment; may guide therapy modification
data.residual_mass: Common in lymphoma; PET determines metabolic activity
data.thymic_rebound: May mimic residual disease on PET in young patients

items.name: indication
items.data: Multiple Myeloma

items.name: reference
items.data: Kumar et al. Lancet Oncol 2016

data.serum_free_light_chain: Involved FLC ≥10 mg/dL with abnormal ratio

sCR.name: Stringent Complete Response
criteria: Absence of clonal plasma cells by immunohistochemistry or flow cytometry

CR.name: Complete Response
criteria: Negative immunofixation on serum and urine

VGPR.name: Very Good Partial Response
criteria: Serum and urine M-protein detectable by immunofixation but not electrophoresis

PR.name: Partial Response
criteria: AND ≥90% reduction in 24-hour urine M-protein (or <200 mg/24 hours)
If measurable soft tissue plasmacytoma: ≥50% reduction
If only measurable by FLC: ≥50% decrease in difference between involved and uninvolved FLC

SD.name: Stable Disease
SD.criteria: Not meeting criteria for sCR, CR, VGPR, PR, MR, or PD

PD.name: Progressive Disease
criteria: ≥25% increase from lowest confirmed response in serum M-protein (absolute increase ≥0.5 g/dL)
OR urine M-protein (absolute increase ≥200 mg/24 hours)
OR difference between involved and uninvolved FLC (absolute increase ≥10 mg/dL)
OR bone marrow plasma cell percentage (absolute increase ≥10%)
OR definite new bone lesion or soft tissue plasmacytoma
OR definite increase in existing plasmacytoma or bone lesion

data.mrd_negative: No clonal plasma cells detected at specified sensitivity

data.definition: Contrast-enhancing lesion ≥10mm in two perpendicular diameters

criteria: Complete disappearance of all enhancing measurable disease
Off corticosteroids (or on physiologic replacement only)

OR clear clinical deterioration not attributable to other causes

Criteria met on stable or increased corticosteroid dose

data.definition: Apparent radiologic worsening within 12 weeks of radiation completion that stabilizes/improves without treatment change
data.handling: Continue treatment; confirm progression on subsequent scan ≥4 weeks later

data.definition: Rapid decrease in enhancement after antiangiogenic therapy (e.g., bevacizumab)
data.handling: Monitor T2/FLAIR changes; evaluate non-enhancing tumor progression

data.corticosteroid_use: Must document dose; affects response classification
data.clinical_status: Neurological examination required at each assessment
data.bevacizumab_trials: RANO criteria with emphasis on T2/FLAIR progression

definition: Confirmed by second value ≥3 weeks later
psa_progression.flare_provision: PSA flare in first 12 weeks should not trigger discontinuation

response_categories.CR: Complete disappearance of all measurable soft tissue disease
response_categories.SD: Neither PR nor PD criteria met
response_categories.PD: ≥20% increase in sum of diameters AND ≥5mm absolute increase OR new lesion

progression_definition: ≥2 new bone lesions on first scan post-baseline

flare.definition: Apparent new lesions in first 12 weeks due to treatment effect

data.response: Bone lesions are not considered to respond (only stable or progressing)

soft_tissue_and_bone.PR: Soft tissue PR AND no new bone lesions
soft_tissue_and_bone.SD: Soft tissue SD AND no new bone lesions
soft_tissue_and_bone.PD: Any soft tissue PD OR confirmed bone progression

criteria: ≥20% increase in total tumor burden (sum of all target + new measurable lesions)

data.handling: Measure and add to total tumor burden
data.threshold: New lesion ≥10mm (or ≥15mm for lymph nodes) becomes measurable
data.documentation: Record new lesions separately for analysis

data.irPD: Must confirm progression ≥4 weeks after initial assessment

data.definition: Initial apparent increase in tumor burden followed by response
data.management: Continue treatment if clinically stable; re-assess in 4-8 weeks

Further increase in tumor burden OR additional new lesions

options: Continue treatment and reassess in 4-8 weeks
data.clinical_stability: Patient must be clinically stable to continue beyond iUPD

data.confirmation: Additional new lesions on next scan confirm iCPD

data.non_cr_non_pd: iSD or better achieved before iUPD can be BOR if iUPD not confirmed

Any lesion not present at baseline

data.confirmation: If equivocal, confirm at next assessment

CR.name: Complete Response

PD.confirmation: May require confirmation for clinical trials

data.name: Unconfirmed Response

data.name: Composite of the Cure Rate as Measured by Clinical Response and Outcome at the Early Efficacy Visit Combined With Withdrawal Rate
data.definition: Cure rate and withdrawal rate data points was jointly assessed in a composite endpoint for all participants who received at least one dose of GSK2140944. An adverse event (AE) is any untoward medical occurrence in a participant, temporally associated with the use of medicinal product, which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with the treatment. An SAE is any untoward medical occurrence that, at any dose, results in death, is life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalization or causes its prolongation, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, is a congenital anomaly/birth defect, or is an important medical event.

Participants in the study were evaluated for the following clinical laboratory parameters at the indicated time points: total bilirubin and creatinine. Participants were categorized as "High" for laboratory values above normal (reference) and as "Low" for laboratory values below normal ranges used by the central laboratory.

Participants were evaluated for the following clinical laboratory parameters for blood chemistry at the indicated time points: electrolytes (calcium, chloride, potassium, sodium), cholesterol, triglycerides, and urea/BUN. Participants were categorized as "High" for laboratory values above normal (reference) and as "Low" for laboratory values below normal ranges used by the central laboratory.

Participants in the study were evaluated for the following clinical laboratory parameters of hematology at the indicated time points: platelet count and white blood cell count. Participants were categorized as "High" for laboratory values above normal (reference) and as "Low" for laboratory values below normal ranges used by the central laboratory.

Urinalysis parameters included: Urine Bilirubin (UB), Urine Occult Blood (UOB), Urine Glucose (UG), Urine Ketones (UK), Urine Nitrite (UN), Urine Protein (UP), and Urine Leukocyte Esterase test for detecting White Blood Cell (UWBC). The dipstick was a strip used to detect the presence or absence of these parameters in the urine sample.

Urine samples were collected for the measurement of urine pH by dipstick method at Day 14. Urine pH is an acid-base measurement. pH is measured on a numeric scale ranging from 0 to 14; values on the scale refer to the degree of alkalinity or acidity. A pH of 7 is neutral. A pH less than 7 is acidic, and a pH greater than 7 is basic. Normal urine has a slightly acid pH (5.0 - 6.0).

Urine samples were collected for the measurement of urine specific gravity by dipstick method at Day 14. Urine specific gravity is a measure of the concentration of solutes in the urine and provides information on the kidney's ability to concentrate urine. The concentration of the excreted molecules determines the urine's specific gravity. A urinary specific gravity measurement is a routine part of urinalysis. The reference range is 1.002-1.030.

Measure: Maximum Absolute Value of Gallbladder Ejection Fraction (Emax GEF) During Cholecystokinin (CCK) Infusion, as a Measure of Maximum Effect
Method: Gallbladder ejection fraction (EF) is defined as the reduction in gallbladder volume at any time point from Baseline divided by baseline gallbladder volume and multiplied by 100. Baseline gallbladder volume is the average of the 3 gallbladder volume measurements prior to CCK infusion on Day 4, for each treatment period.

Measure: Area Under the Effect Curve for Gallbladder Ejection Fraction (AUEC GEF)
Method: Gallbladder ultrasonography was done at Day 1 (-15, -10, and -5 minutes [min] relative to start of albiglutide/placebo injection) and Day 4 ([prior to CCK infusion] -15, -10, -5 min, followed by [during CCK infusion] every 5 min between 0 and 50 min, then [after CCK infusion] at 60, 70, and 80 min, relative to the start of CCK infusion). Adjusted mean and its standard error have been presented.

The primary efficacy analysis will be based on PFS as assessed by the IRC. The primary analysis will be performed using a stratified log-rank test stratified by the number of prior systemic therapies for advanced disease (1 vs ≥2) and presence of liver metastases (yes vs no) at a one-sided significance level of 0.025.

The distribution of PFS will be estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Kaplan-Meier curves will be presented by treatment group and by subgroups defined by stratification factors. Median PFS and corresponding 95% confidence intervals will be provided for each treatment group.

The hazard ratio and corresponding 95% confidence interval will be estimated using a stratified Cox proportional hazards model stratified by the number of prior systemic therapies for advanced disease (1 vs ≥2) and presence of liver metastases (yes vs no).

data.text: The primary endpoints, Cmax and AUC0-t in fasting or fed group, will be log-transformed and a mixed-effects model will be applied. The model will include fixed effects for sequence, treatment, and period and a random effect of subject nested within sequence. Treatment differences on the log scale will be estimated for the parameters together with their 90% CIs. The least squares means together with their 95% CIs by treatment will also be estimated. Point estimates and CIs will be back-transformed to the original scale for presentation, i.e., ratios of geometric means and corresponding 90% CIs for Treatment A/Treatment B, geometric means and corresponding 95% CIs by treatment, respectively.
The mixed trapezoidal rule will be used to calculate the area under the plasma concentration curve.
Pharmacokinetic parameters (primary and secondary endpoints) will be calculated according to non-compartmental analysis methods.
For tmax, the Hodges-Lehmann estimates for the treatment differences and corresponding 90% CIs according to the Tukey method will be calculated.

Terminal elimination rate constant. Determined from the terminal slope of the log-transformed concentration curve using linear regression on terminal data points of the curve. The regression analysis should contain data from at least 3 different time points in the terminal phase consistent with the assessment of a straight line on the log-transformed scale. Phoenix WinNonlin best fit methodology will be used as standard. The Rsq should be ≥0.800 and the observation period over which the regression line is estimated should be at least two-fold the resulting t1/2 itself.

If subjects receive concomitant medication that potentially affects PK for the treatment of an AE, their inclusion in the PK Analysis Set will be decided on a case-by-case basis. Emesis occurring within two times of the median tmax for a given analyte and the treatment will be considered a relevant event likely to affect the comparability of PK results. Similarly, a predose concentration for a given analyte and treatment period which exceeds 5% of Cmax will be considered a relevant event affecting PK results. All PK analyses will be based on the PK Analysis Set.

The primary analysis of efficacy will be performed using the ITT population. The change from baseline to in PDSS will be compared between HB-1 and placebo using Mixed Model Repeated Measures (MMRM) model using SAS mixed procedure with repeated measures. The model will include the fixed effect of treatment, visit, the treatment-by-visit interaction, baseline, baseline-by-visit. The outcome will be the change from baseline to each on-treatment time point. All protocol-scheduled time points will be included in the model. The model will use the unstructured or Toeplitz (whichever has a better fit by AICC value) within-subject variance-covariance matrix. The denominator degrees of freedom will be according to the method of Kenward-Roger.

To control for multiplicity of select analyses, Hochberg's procedure will be used to test the protocol designated primary endpoint (PDSS) as well as the key secondary endpoint CGI-S, which are not expected to be negatively correlated. Accordingly, if the largest p-value among these two endpoints (at the primary time point) does not exceed 0.05, then both endpoints will be considered statistically significant. If the largest p-value exceeds 0.05 and the smallest p-value does not exceed 0.025, then the endpoint with the smaller p-values will be considered statistically significant. This provides control of the familywise error rate at α = 0.05 such that either of the 2 endpoints statistically significant according to the above procedure will constitute a successful efficacy outcome for the trial.

{
  "text": "The PK Analysis Set includes all subjects who completed the trial with adequate trial medication compliance, without any relevant protocol violations or events with respect to factors likely to affect the comparability of PK results, and with sufficient evaluable data to determine primary endpoints (AUC0-t and Cmax) for both treatments and analytes. If subjects receive concomitant medication that potentially affects PK for the treatment of an AE, their inclusion in the PK Analysis Set will be decided on a case-by-case basis. Emesis occurring within two times of the median tmax for a given analyte and the treatment will be considered a relevant event likely to affect the comparability of PK results. Similarly, a predose concentration for a given analyte and treatment period which exceeds 5% of Cmax will be considered a relevant event affecting PK results. pipeline.description: Combines Knowledge Graph extraction with SELF-RAG verification for accurate SAP generation

stages.name: KG Extraction
stages.description: Extract structured facts from protocol using Claude with knowledge graph

stages.name: Dynamic SAP Structure
stages.description: Determine required SAP sections based on protocol characteristics

stages.name: Knowledge Base Tools Selection
stages.description: Select and invoke appropriate KB tools for each SAP section

files_used.usage: KnowledgeBaseTools class - main access layer to all KB content

stages.name: Statistical Methods Retrieval
stages.description: Retrieve statistical analysis methods based on endpoint types

stages.name: Response Criteria Retrieval
stages.description: Get disease-specific response criteria (RECIST, Lugano, IWG-AML, etc.)

stages.name: Therapy-Specific Content
stages.description: Retrieve therapy-specific endpoints and safety monitoring

stages.name: TFL Shell Generation
stages.description: Generate Table, Figure, Listing shells for SAP

stages.name: Similar Trial Lookup
stages.description: Find similar trials in the factual KG for precedent data

stages.name: Power Calculation
stages.description: Calculate sample size and power using scipy

stages.name: RAG Style Context
stages.description: Retrieve similar SAP examples for prose style reference

stages.name: SELF-RAG Verification
stages.description: Verify generated SAP against extracted facts

stages.name: Correction Loop
stages.description: If verification fails, regenerate with corrections

stages.name: Final SAP Output
stages.description: Final SAP with audit trail and provenance
